Definition: from G4119; to do, make or be more, i.e. increase (transitively or intransitively); by extension, to superabound:--abound, abundant, make to increase, have over.
BiblicalUsage: Pleonazo means to abound, to increase beyond measure. Where sin abounded, grace did much more abound, says Romans 5:20 — and Romans 6:1 answers the fool who asks, shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? Paul prays the Thessalonians' love may increase in 1 Thessalonians 3:12, and says thanksgiving abounds through many in 2 Corinthians 4:15.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe grace out-abounds sin every time, and that is not a licence to sin but the reason not to. My position is that the more grace abounds, the more love should abound too.
